text:
sanjay: Heads-up — we're starting to spec the per-route SLO dashboards for latency/throughput (P50/P95/P99, TTFT, tokens/sec). Need runtime + infra inputs for metric names, label cardinality, and sampling strategy. Who's available to sync?

amanda: I can join. Quick Q: do we want model+route together in one dashboard or separate panels per model?

sanjay: Prefer one dashboard that can group/filter by model_id, route_id, deployment_variant, and region. Panels per metric (latency/ttft/tokens/sec) with a top-level selector. Keeps UX compact.

jo: +1. Also need to know how runtime will emit latency — histograms or summaries? cardinality of route labels matters for Prometheus.

rick: Runtime currently emits route_latency_bucket (Histogram) with labels: route, model, variant, region, priority. token_rate is a gauge emitted per instance and aggregated by route/model. TTFT is a counter that we compute by tracking first_token_timestamp - request_start_timestamp (we emit ttft_ms gauge per request sampled).

emily: Sampling detail: to control cardinality we sample 1% for verbose labels, and 100% for route/model/region. Is that still the plan?

rick: Yes. We keep high-cardinality labels out of the primary metric stream. The histogram buckets are pre-defined: [5,10,25,50,100,200,500,1000,2000] ms.

telemetry-bot: NOTE: ingest quota for high-cardinality metrics may trigger spike protections. See policy #metrics-cardinality on the docs site.

amanda: Ok — UX asks: panels should show P50/P95/P99, and a separate TTFT panel with P50/P95. Also tokens/sec as rolling 1m and 5m. We need PromQL examples to hand to console for panel wiring.

rick: PromQL examples (rough):

```
# P95 latency per route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(route_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model, variant, region))

# tokens/sec per route (1m window)
sum(rate(tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (route, model, variant, region)

# TTFT P50 per route (we emit ttft_ms as a gauge sample)
quantile_over_time(0.5, ttft_ms[5m]) by (route, model, variant, region)
```

jo: That looks good. Couple notes: histogram_quantile in Prometheus needs correct bucket alignment; runtime should guarantee consistent buckets across deployments.

rick: Confirmed — same bucket config across all runtime fleets.

amanda: For the console panels we also need a downsampled rollup for 1h/6h/24h to avoid slow frontend queries. Can platform supply pre-aggregated rollups?

rick: We have a rollup job in infra that computes hourly aggregates into metrics_rollup.series (sum/count/histogram_agg). I'll add a tag so console can query rollup: rollup=1h.

emily: Cost question — histogram buckets and per-route label increases TSDB cardinality. Are we comfortable on the long-term retention?

telemetry-bot: Current quotas: metrics_store retention default 30d for raw histograms; rollups stored 180d. Over-quota alerts will post to #eng-infra.

amanda: Nice. Panel UX: default view = all models combined; user can filter by model or route. We also want to surface a "regression" badge if P95 increases by >20% week-over-week. Can we get weekly baseline?

rick: We can compute baseline using weekly_rollup or compare current 7d avg vs previous 7d avg. Backend is able to return percent_change. Example PromQL-ish approach:

```
(current = avg_over_time(p95_query[7d]))
(previous = avg_over_time(p95_query offset 7d[7d]))
100 * (current - previous) / previous
```

jo: We'll need to limit how many routes are computed for regression checks to avoid large query fanout. Maybe only top N by traffic + any pinned routes.

sanjay: Agreed. Action items coming out of this thread: 1) Runtime (rick) — publish exact metric names + labels + bucket config in repo (deadline EOD Friday). 2) Infra (emily) — confirm retention & rollup cadence, and add rollup tag (deadline Mon). 3) Console (amanda/jo) — draft panel spec with sample PromQL and pagination/filter UX (deadline next Wed). 4) Platform (sanjay) — document alert thresholds and regression logic (deadline next Wed).

amanda: I'll own the panel spec. Will put a PR on console repo and tag the group.

rick: I'll open a runtime PR with metric names and a prometheus config snippet.

emily: I'll check retention numbers and update metrics quota doc.

telemetry-bot: Reminder: Please include the metrics contract template when publishing names. Template: metric_name, type, labels(list), cardinality_est, retention, rollup.

jo: One more UX thing — TTFT definition needs to be exact: "time from request.start to first token emitted by model" measured at the ingress point to include network and CPU scheduling. Rick can you confirm where ttft is measured?

rick: We'll measure TTFT at the runtime ingress just after request parsing, and first_token_time when we push to outbound stream. That will include serving overhead but not client network. Added to the PR notes.

sanjay: Great. Last: can we schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to walk the panel draft and metric names? 10:30am PT works for me.

amanda: Works. I'll add a calendar invite and include the console + runtime + infra leads. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

emily: Added. I'll bring retention numbers.

rick: I'll bring bucket config and sample metrics from staging.

jo: See you. I'll sketch the dashboard layout beforehand.

sanjay: Thanks all — filing this as the owner thread for the route-level SLO dashboard effort. Will post link to PRs here as they land. :thumbsup:
